german_characters.name: Erich von Falkenhayn
german_characters.rank: General der Infanterie (Chief of General Staff)
german_characters.background: Career officer, former War Minister. Architect of Verdun offensive ('Operation Gericht').
german_characters.physical: Stern face, close-cropped hair, monocle. Prussian bearing.
german_characters.personality: Cold, calculating. Believes in attrition warfare. Theoretical rather than empathetic.
german_characters.fate: Resigned August 1916 after Verdun/Somme failures. Commanded in Romania, Turkey. Died 1922.
german_characters.narrative_arc: The architect—distant, strategic. Responsibility without presence.
german_characters.philosophy: 'The string in France has reached breaking point. A mass break-through—which in any case is beyond our means—is unnecessary. Within our reach there are objectives for the retention of which the French would be compelled to throw in every man they have. If they do so, the forces of France will bleed to death.'
relationships: Opposed by Crown Prince Wilhelm (operational level)
german_characters.historical_note: Real person. 'Christmas Memorandum' outlined Verdun strategy (disputed authenticity).

german_characters.name: Wilhelm, Crown Prince of Prussia
german_characters.background: Kaiser Wilhelm II's eldest son. Educated for military command but largely figurehead. Actual decisions made by Chief of Staff Schmidt von Knobelsdorf.
german_characters.physical: Tall, athletic, high forehead, prominent chin. Hussars uniform.
german_characters.personality: Ambitious, vain, but not without conscience. Privately doubts Verdun strategy. Publicly bound by duty.
german_characters.fate: Survived WWI. Renounced succession rights 1918. Died 1951.
german_characters.narrative_arc: Reluctant commander—prestige without power. Scapegoat for failure.
relationships: Blamed by soldiers for Verdun casualties
german_characters.internal_conflict: Doubted Verdun offensive before it began but could not oppose father/Falkenhayn.
german_characters.historical_note: Real person. Memoirs suggest he opposed Verdun plan.

german_characters.name: Konstantin Schmidt von Knobelsdorf
german_characters.unit: Chief of Staff, German Fifth Army
german_characters.background: Career staff officer. True operational mind behind Fifth Army. Aggressive advocate of Verdun offensive.
german_characters.physical: Barrel-chested, graying hair, thick mustache. Intense eyes.
german_characters.personality: Stubborn, aggressive, dismissive of casualties. 'Victory or annihilation.'
german_characters.fate: Removed from command August 1916. Retired. Died 1936.
german_characters.narrative_arc: True believer—pushes offensive beyond reason.
german_characters.famous_quote: 'The heart of France beats at Verdun. We will tear it out.'
german_characters.historical_note: Real person. Blamed for prolonging failed offensive.

german_characters.name: Ernst von Hoeppner
german_characters.background: Aviation pioneer. Organized air reconnaissance and combat operations at Verdun.
german_characters.physical: Lean, sharp features, aviator's scarf even on ground.
german_characters.personality: Innovative, modern thinker. Advocates for aircraft as offensive weapon, not just reconnaissance.
german_characters.fate: Survived war. Died 1922.
german_characters.narrative_arc: Modernist—represents future of warfare.
german_characters.tactical_innovation: Coordinated fighter sweeps ('Jagdstaffeln') to contest French air superiority.
german_characters.historical_note: Real person. Luftstreitkräfte commander 1916.

german_characters.name: Oswald Boelcke
german_characters.background: Pre-eminent fighter ace. 40 victories by October 1916. Created air combat tactics.
german_characters.physical: Blonde, blue-eyed, boyish face. Small build.
german_characters.personality: Methodical, cerebral. Wrote 'Dicta Boelcke' (combat principles). Humble despite fame.
german_characters.fate: Killed in mid-air collision, October 28, 1916 (over Somme, not Verdun). National mourning.
german_characters.narrative_arc: The knight—chivalric warrior in mechanized war. Death shows modernity's indifference.
german_characters.historical_note: Real person. Not killed at Verdun but temporally/thematically relevant.

german_characters.name: Max Immelmann
german_characters.background: Pioneer of aerial combat. 'Eagle of Lille.' Created 'Immelmann turn' maneuver.
german_characters.physical: Thin, intellectual appearance. Fokker Eindecker pilot.
german_characters.personality: Thoughtful, technical. Less flamboyant than Boelcke but equally skilled.
german_characters.fate: Killed June 18, 1916 (over Lens, not Verdun). Cause disputed: British fire or structural failure.
german_characters.narrative_arc: Parallel to Boelcke—modernity's champions, modernity's victims.
german_characters.historical_note: Real person. Included for aerial warfare context.

german_characters.name: Friedrich Steinbrecher
german_characters.background: Theology student pre-war. Volunteered 1914 from idealism. Progressively disillusioned.
german_characters.physical: Dark-haired, slight build, wire-rimmed glasses. Scholar's face.
german_characters.personality: Introspective, sensitive. Keeps detailed diary. Questions meaning of suffering.
german_characters.fate: Survived Verdun. Later fought at Somme. Died of illness 1918 (influenza).
german_characters.narrative_arc: Intellectual witness—German counterpart to French diarists (Pézard, Laby).
diary_entries: 'Verdun transforms men into beasts or stones. I fear I am becoming the latter.'
'God is silent here. Perhaps He cannot bear to watch.'
relationships: Befriends enlisted men despite officer status
german_characters.historical_note: Real person. Actual Verdun diarist. Diary published posthumously.

german_characters.name: Ernst Jünger
german_characters.background: Ran away to Foreign Legion pre-war. Returned, enlisted. Wounded multiple times.
german_characters.physical: Lean, intense eyes, aristocratic features.
german_characters.personality: Aestheticizes violence. Sees war as transcendent experience. Cold observer, passionate participant.
german_characters.fate: Survived WWI (wounded 14 times). Post-war: Author ('Storm of Steel'). Lived to 102 (died 1998).
german_characters.narrative_arc: The poet of war—finds beauty in horror. Controversial figure.
relationships: Distant from those who want only survival
german_characters.philosophy: 'War is the father of all things.' (quoting Heraclitus)
german_characters.historical_note: Real person. Not specifically at Verdun but emblematic of German war literature.

german_characters.name: Wilhelm Hosenfeld
german_characters.background: Farm boy. Devout Catholic. Volunteered underage (lied about age).
german_characters.physical: Blonde, tall for age, still growing. Open face.
german_characters.personality: Naive, earnest. Believes in duty to Kaiser and God. War will shatter him.
german_characters.fate: Survived Verdun (wounded July). Later: Wehrmacht WWII, saved Jews in Warsaw. Died Soviet POW camp 1952.
german_characters.narrative_arc: Innocence corrupted, later redeemed (WWII context beyond game).
relationships: Protected by older soldiers in unit
german_characters.historical_note: Real person (WWII rescuer). Composite WWI youth archetype.

german_characters.name: Karl von Müller
german_characters.background: Pioneer of stormtrooper tactics. Trained in infiltration, grenade assault, flamethrowers.
german_characters.physical: Scarred face (flamethrower accident), muscular build. Missing half of left ear.
german_characters.personality: Aggressive, innovative, brutal. Leads from front. Respects competence, not rank.
german_characters.fate: Survived Verdun. Killed 1918, Spring Offensive.
german_characters.narrative_arc: The new soldier—represents tactical evolution. Brutality as professionalism.
german_characters.tactical_focus: Close-quarters combat, grenade tactics, rapid infiltration.
german_characters.historical_note: Composite of stormtrooper officers (Rohr Battalion active at Verdun).

german_characters.name: Hans-Joachim Wolff
german_characters.background: Bank clerk. Mobilized 1914. Participated in capture of Fort Douaumont Feb 25, 1916.
german_characters.physical: Medium build, brown hair, nervous tic (left eye twitches).
german_characters.personality: Ordinary, unremarkable. Neither hero nor coward. Survives by luck and caution.
german_characters.fate: Survived Verdun. Wounded August 1916 (minor). Survived war. Returned to banking.
german_characters.narrative_arc: The survivor—represents mass of soldiers who simply endured.
relationships: Part of patrol that entered Douaumont
german_characters.internal_thought: 'I was there. I did not flee. That is enough.'
german_characters.historical_note: Fictional composite. Brandenburg Regiment did capture Douaumont.

german_characters.name: Eugen Radtke
german_characters.background: Led patrol that captured Fort Douaumont. Later disputed as hero by Sergeant Kunze.
german_characters.physical: Stocky, blonde, square jaw.
german_characters.personality: Ambitious, eager for glory. Disputes over credit for Douaumont embitter him.
german_characters.fate: Survived Verdun. Survived war. Controversy over Douaumont credit followed him.
german_characters.narrative_arc: Glory-seeker—undone by ambiguity of heroism.
relationships: Rivalry with Sgt. Kunze over Douaumont credit
german_characters.historical_note: Real person (likely). Capture of Douaumont disputed among Germans themselves.

german_characters.name: Georg Bucher
german_characters.background: Pre-war miner. Expertise in tunneling, demolitions, underground warfare.
german_characters.physical: Broad-shouldered, coal-dust permanently in skin creases. Missing right index finger (mining accident).
german_characters.personality: Practical, dark humor. Comfortable underground. Claustrophobia in open spaces.
german_characters.fate: Killed May 12, 1916, tunnel collapse during mine warfare under Fort Vaux.
german_characters.narrative_arc: The miner—war beneath the war. Buried alive, ironic given profession.
german_characters.last_moments: Trapped in darkness. Sings Württemberg folk song until air runs out.
german_characters.historical_note: Composite. Extensive mine warfare at Verdun (less famous than Somme mines).

german_characters.name: Otto Dix
german_characters.background: Art student pre-war. Volunteered 1914. Drew sketches of war.
german_characters.physical: Sharp features, intense eyes, ink-stained hands.
german_characters.personality: Observes horror clinically. Draws what he sees. Art as testimony.
german_characters.fate: Survived Verdun. Survived war. Post-war: Expressionist painter of WWI trauma ('Der Krieg', 1924). Persecuted by Nazis. Died 1969.
german_characters.narrative_arc: Artist-witness—transforms trauma into art.
relationships: Respected for bravery despite artistic temperament
german_characters.artistic_focus: Sketches corpses, wounded, landscapes of devastation.
german_characters.historical_note: Real person. Fought on Western Front including Somme. Verdun link uncertain but thematically appropriate.

german_characters.name: Paul Bäumer
german_characters.background: Student, encouraged to enlist by schoolmaster. Idealistic, soon shattered.
german_characters.physical: Youthful, thin, haunted eyes.
german_characters.personality: Sensitive, questioning. Bonds deeply with comrades. Philosophically lost.
german_characters.fate: Killed October 1918 (not Verdun—Western Front). 'Fell on a day so quiet the army report confined itself to: All Quiet on the Western Front.'
german_characters.narrative_arc: The lost generation—symbolic figure (from Remarque novel).
relationships: Fictional character from Remarque's novel, included as cultural touchstone
german_characters.historical_note: Fictional (Remarque's 'All Quiet on the Western Front', 1928). Included as literary reference.

german_characters.name: Theodor Plievier
german_characters.unit: Transferred to infantry from Kaiserliche Marine
german_characters.background: Socialist sympathies. Skeptical of war. Observes absurdity.
german_characters.physical: Wiry, sardonic expression.
german_characters.personality: Cynical, anti-authoritarian. Later becomes anti-war writer.
german_characters.fate: Survived war. Participated in Kiel Mutiny 1918. Emigrated. Wrote war novels ('Stalingrad', 'Moscow').
german_characters.narrative_arc: The dissident—voice of disillusionment.
german_characters.historical_note: Real person. Writer, sailor. Included for political dimension.

german_characters.name: Ludwig Renn
german_characters.background: Aristocrat turned socialist. Officer from class obligation, soldier from duty.
german_characters.physical: Tall, refined features, patrician bearing.
german_characters.personality: Intellectual, conflicted by class and ideology. Observes war's class dimensions.
german_characters.fate: Survived war. Joined Communist Party. Fought in Spanish Civil War (International Brigades). Died 1979 (East Germany).
german_characters.narrative_arc: Class traitor—rejects aristocratic militarism.
relationships: Respected by working-class soldiers despite nobility
german_characters.historical_note: Real person. WWI veteran, later communist. Published memoir 'War' (1928).

german_characters.name: Anton Schnack
german_characters.background: Poet. Volunteered 1915. Wounded multiple times.
german_characters.physical: Dark-haired, slight, introspective eyes.
german_characters.personality: Romantic turned realist. Poetry becomes vehicle for trauma.
german_characters.fate: Survived war. Published poetry collection 'Tier rang gewaltig mit Tier' (Beast Fought Mightily with Beast, 1920). Died 1973.
german_characters.narrative_arc: Poet-soldier—language fails, persists anyway.
german_characters.poetry_themes: Corporeal horror, landscape as corpse, silence of God.
german_characters.historical_note: Real person. WWI poet.

german_characters.name: Rudolf Binding
german_characters.background: Aristocratic officer, writer. Older, reflective observer.
german_characters.physical: Gray-haired, monocle, upright posture.
german_characters.personality: Old-school honor code. Horrified by industrial war but maintains composure.
german_characters.fate: Survived war. Published war diary 'A Fatalist at War' (1927). Died 1938.
german_characters.narrative_arc: The anachronism—chivalric values in unchivalric war.
german_characters.diary_style: Measured, classical prose. Elegy for lost world.
german_characters.historical_note: Real person. WWI cavalry officer and writer.

german_characters.name: Walter Flex
german_characters.background: Writer, poet. Nationalist idealist. Believed in spiritual meaning of war.
german_characters.physical: Blonde, athletic, Nordic features.
german_characters.personality: Idealistic, saw war as purifying. Earnest belief in German cultural mission.
german_characters.fate: Killed October 16, 1917 (Øsel Island, Baltic). Became nationalist martyr.
german_characters.narrative_arc: The believer—nationalism as faith. Death sanctifies ideology.
german_characters.famous_work: 'Der Wanderer zwischen beiden Welten' (The Wanderer Between Two Worlds, 1917). Bestseller in Nazi era.
german_characters.historical_note: Real person. Not at Verdun but ideological counterpoint to disillusioned writers.

german_characters.name: August Stramm
german_characters.background: Expressionist poet. Pioneered radical syntax and compression. Postal official pre-war.
german_characters.physical: Balding, intense gaze, weathered face.
german_characters.personality: Intense, experimental. Language as weapon against horror.
german_characters.fate: Killed September 1, 1915 (Eastern Front, before Verdun). Included as literary figure.
german_characters.narrative_arc: Language destroyed—war breaks syntax, meaning.
german_characters.poetry_example: 'Patrouille' (Patrol): radical compression, neologisms, disintegration of grammar mirroring war's disintegration of reality.
german_characters.historical_note: Real person. Expressionist WWI poet.

german_characters.name: Heinrich Böll
german_characters.background: Post-WWI generation. Served WWII. Post-war novelist of war's trauma.
german_characters.fate: Lived 1917-1985. Nobel Prize 1972. Wrote about both wars' legacies.
german_characters.narrative_arc: Next generation—inherits trauma.
german_characters.historical_note: Real person. Born 1917. Included as generational bridge (Verdun's legacy affects next generation).

german_characters.name: Werner Beumelburg
german_characters.background: War correspondent, soldier. Later nationalist writer.
german_characters.physical: Compact build, journalist's observant eyes.
german_characters.personality: Nationalist, but honest about war's horror. Conservative romanticism.
german_characters.fate: Survived war. Wrote nationalistic war novels ('Gruppe Bosemüller', 1930). Died 1963.
german_characters.narrative_arc: The chronicler—nationalist perspective.
german_characters.historical_note: Real person. WWI soldier and writer.

german_characters.name: Manfred von Richthofen
german_characters.background: Cavalry officer, transferred to aviation 1915. Trained by Boelcke. Became top ace (80 victories).
german_characters.physical: Blonde, blue eyes, slender. Red Fokker Dr.I triplane.
german_characters.personality: Cool, calculating hunter. Professional killer, not romantic knight. Collected trophies.
german_characters.fate: Killed April 21, 1918 (Somme sector). National icon.
german_characters.narrative_arc: The ace—modernity's knight, modernity's product.
german_characters.historical_note: Real person. Active late 1916 onward. 'Red Baron.'

german_characters.name: Hermann Löns
german_characters.background: Naturalist writer, journalist. Volunteered despite age. Romanticized German landscape and 'Volk.'
german_characters.physical: Middle-aged, graying, weathered face.
german_characters.personality: Romantic nationalist. Saw war as defense of German soil and culture.
german_characters.fate: Killed September 26, 1914 (Reims, very early in war). Body lost. Reburied 1935 (Nazi ceremony, disputed remains).
german_characters.narrative_arc: Early martyr—romantic nationalism dies first.
german_characters.historical_note: Real person. Killed before Verdun but ideological icon co-opted by Nazis.
